headline: 4 killed as bus and battery rickshaw collide in Mirpur
summary: The head-on collision occurred on the Beribadh embankment road near Nawabbagh Uttarpara around 7:30am on Wednesday.
details: A bus rammed into a battery-operated rickshaw on the Beribadh embankment road in Dhaka’s Mirpur area, leaving four people dead.
The Fire Service and Civil Defence confirmed the casualties, noting that the victims include two men and two women.
The accident took place around 7:30am on Wednesday near Nawabbagh Uttarpara.
A unit from the Kalyanpur Fire Station carried out the rescue operation at the scene to recover the victims.
caption:
4 people dead after a bus and battery rickshaw collided head-on in Mirpur.

A bus rammed into a battery-operated rickshaw on the Beribadh embankment road in Dhaka’s Mirpur area, leaving four people dead.

The Fire Service and Civil Defence confirmed the casualties, noting that the victims include two men and two women.

The accident took place around 7:30am on Wednesday near Nawabbagh Uttarpara.

A unit from the Kalyanpur Fire Station carried out the rescue operation at the scene to recover the victims.

headline: Democrat Roy Cooper flips Republican-held US Senate seat in North Carolina
summary: Former governor Roy Cooper defeated Trump-backed Michael Whatley, providing a crucial pickup for Democrats in their bid for Senate control.
details: Democrat Roy Cooper won North Carolina’s US Senate race on Tuesday, according to media projections, defeating Trump-backed Republican Michael Whatley.
Cooper, a former two-term governor, campaigned on the high cost of food and energy as President Donald Trump's approval ratings declined.
The victory is a crucial pickup for Democrats, who need a net gain of four seats to take control of the Senate, where Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority.
Cooper, 69, will replace retiring Republican Senator Thom Tillis, who stepped down after breaking with Trump over Medicaid cuts.
With strong statewide name recognition and support from independent voters, Cooper maintained a significant polling lead throughout the campaign.
His opponent, Michael Whatley, a former Republican National Committee chair who has never held elective office, campaigned alongside Donald Trump.
Whatley previously led an RNC election integrity drive to place 100,000 volunteers and attorneys in battleground states to monitor voting.
caption:
A major shift in North Carolina: Democrat Roy Cooper has flipped a Republican US Senate seat.

Democrat Roy Cooper won North Carolina’s US Senate race on Tuesday, according to media projections, defeating Trump-backed Republican Michael Whatley.

Cooper, a former two-term governor, campaigned on the high cost of food and energy as President Donald Trump's approval ratings declined.

The victory is a crucial pickup for Democrats, who need a net gain of four seats to take control of the Senate, where Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority.

Cooper, 69, will replace retiring Republican Senator Thom Tillis, who stepped down after breaking with Trump over Medicaid cuts.

With strong statewide name recognition and support from independent voters, Cooper maintained a significant polling lead throughout the campaign.

His opponent, Michael Whatley, a former Republican National Committee chair who has never held elective office, campaigned alongside Donald Trump.

Whatley previously led an RNC election integrity drive to place 100,000 volunteers and attorneys in battleground states to monitor voting.
